evidence: create-cart.interactor.ts: CreateCartInteractor implements CreateCartInPort and gets SaveCartOutPort and CreateSagaOutPort through its constructor; it calls cart.createOrder(sagaId, correlationId) and then saveCartPort.saveCart(cart).

update-cart.interactor.ts: UpdateCartInteractor implements UpdateCartInPort and gets SaveCartOutPort and GetCartOutPort through its constructor; it calls getCartOutPort.getCart, then cart.cancelOrder(), then saveCartPort.saveCart(cart).
Both files save through the same SaveCartOutPort and leave state changes to CartEntity, so no invariant is duplicated.
Smaller problem: create-cart.interactor.ts hard-codes test CartPositionEntity items (names 'hah1', 'hah2', 'hah3'; codes 1001, 1002, 1004).
Smaller problem: UpdateCartInteractor.execute only cancels the order, which doesn't match its general 'update' name.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The unit passes. Both interactors handle one concern: cart use cases in the hexagonal domain. Each one implements an inbound port, depends only on injected outbound ports (SaveCartOutPort, GetCartOutPort, CreateSagaOutPort), and leaves state changes to CartEntity methods (createOrder, cancelOrder). Neither file reaches persistence or the saga service directly, so the module's own abstractions are not bypassed. No rule or invariant appears in both files; order creation and cancellation rules stay inside CartEntity.

Two smaller problems don't break the rubric. CreateCartInteractor builds the cart from hard-coded test line items ('hah1', 'hah2', 'hah3'). UpdateCartInteractor is named as a general update but only cancels the order.
